root_cause.text: The rxe driver incorrectly assumed that MR page size equals PAGE_SIZE, so it stored only system page pointers in an xarray without accounting for offsets or splitting when MR page size differs, causing incorrect iova-to-va conversion.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly describes two scenarios (page_size < PAGE_SIZE and page_size > PAGE_SIZE) where the old indexing and offset calculations produce wrong virtual addresses, e.g., "Before fix: ... Resulting VA: 0x170010 (wrong)" while the expected VA is 0x173010 for the first case. The patch replaces the xarray with an array of `rxe_mr_page` structures that include both a page pointer and an offset, and modifies `rxe_mr_iova_to_index` and `rxe_mr_iova_to_page_offset` to handle the page size mismatch correctly.

candidates.rationale: This index calculation assumes each index corresponds to one MR page, but the xarray stores one system page per index. When MR page size differs from PAGE_SIZE, the index does not map correctly to the stored system page pointers, leading to incorrect page retrieval.

This stores a single system page pointer into the xarray at the current index. Since the indices are based on MR page size, but each system page is stored separately, multiple system pages that belong to the same MR page are placed at consecutive indices instead of being grouped. This mismatch causes incorrect iova-to-va translation when MR page size > PAGE_SIZE.

This stores one system page per incrementing index (nbuf). It assumes that each call to rxe_set_page corresponds to a single system page, but the MR page size may be larger. Consequently, a single MR page span is not represented by a single xarray entry, leading to out-of-bounds access when using iova-to-page offset calculations.

This loads a page pointer from the xarray using an MR-page-based index. However, the stored page is only the first system page of the MR page. When the page_offset exceeds a single system page, the code accesses memory beyond the mapped page, causing incorrect data or crashes.

This maps the loaded system page into kernel address space. Combined with the offset page_offset (which may be larger than PAGE_SIZE), the subsequent memcpy accesses memory outside the mapped page, leading to incorrect iova-to-va conversion when MR page size > PAGE_SIZE.

Same pattern in check_rkey: the page pointer retrieved from the xarray is insufficient to handle offsets that span multiple system pages, leading to incorrect validation and potential memory corruption.
